CH01_SC01_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC01_001_NARRATOR.text: Golden hour settles over Umm Al Emarat Park in Abu Dhabi. Beneath the competition tents, young dessert makers race to complete their final creations. Utensils move, mixers turn, and carefully measured ingredients become the final dishes that will soon be presented to the judges.
CH01_SC01_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC01_002_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC01_002_NARRATOR.text: At one preparation station, two finalists are approaching the most important moment of their competition. Mariam Al Mansoori and Saeed Al Nuaimi are close to completing their dessert. But time is running out. Only twelve minutes remain before the final judging round.
CH01_SC01_002_NARRATOR.direction: Cinematic, measured. Pause before “Only twelve minutes remain.”
CH01_SC01_002_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC02_001_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH01_SC02_001_MARIAM.text: Saeed, we are almost finished. I need the sugar and the baking soda for the final stage.
CH01_SC02_001_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC02_002_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH01_SC02_002_SAEED.text: I’ll get them now. The judges could arrive at any moment.
CH01_SC02_002_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC02_003_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC02_003_NARRATOR.text: The recipe is clear. The equipment is ready. Each person knows what must be done. At this moment, the challenge appears to be about speed. But within seconds, it will become a question of evidence, scientific reasoning, and food safety.
CH01_SC02_003_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC03_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC03_001_NARRATOR.text: On the preparation counter are three sealed containers. Each container holds a fine white powder. Their identification labels are attached, and the ingredients appear to be ready for use.
CH01_SC03_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC03_002_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC03_002_NARRATOR.text: One container holds sucrose, commonly known as table sugar. Another holds sodium hydrogen carbonate, commonly known as baking soda. The third holds sodium chloride, or table salt. Visually, however, the three powders are remarkably similar.
CH01_SC03_002_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC04_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC04_001_NARRATOR.text: Then, without warning, the identification labels begin to detach.
CH01_SC04_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC04_002_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC04_002_NARRATOR.text: One falls. Then another. Then the third.
CH01_SC04_002_NARRATOR.direction: Synchronize each phrase with one falling label.
CH01_SC04_002_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC04_003_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH01_SC04_003_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC04_004_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC04_004_NARRATOR.text: In only a few seconds, three clearly identified ingredients become three anonymous white powders.
CH01_SC04_004_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC04_005_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH01_SC04_005_SAEED.text: I can’t tell which container is which.
CH01_SC04_005_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC05_001_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH01_SC05_001_SAEED.text: They all look almost exactly the same. One should be sugar, one should be baking soda, and one should be salt, but the labels are no longer connected to the containers.
CH01_SC05_001_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC05_002_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH01_SC05_002_MARIAM.text: We cannot guess. Using the wrong ingredient could ruin the recipe.
CH01_SC05_002_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC05_003_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC05_003_NARRATOR.text: The containers remain sealed. No one has tasted the powders, and none of the unknown materials has been added to the food. No injury has occurred. No contamination has been confirmed. But the chain of identification has been broken.
CH01_SC05_003_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC05_004_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC05_004_NARRATOR.text: What began as a simple preparation problem is now a food-safety problem.
CH01_SC05_004_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC06_001_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH01_SC06_001_FATIMA.text: Stop preparation immediately. Do not open or use any of those containers.
CH01_SC06_001_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC06_002_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH01_SC06_002_SAEED.text: Even if we think we know which one is the sugar?
CH01_SC06_002_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC06_003_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH01_SC06_003_FATIMA.text: Thinking is not enough. The ingredients are no longer reliably identified. Until we have defensible evidence and a safe course of action, they must remain isolated.
CH01_SC06_003_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC06_004_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH01_SC06_004_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC06_005_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC06_005_NARRATOR.text: Fatima makes the responsible decision, even though the final judging round is approaching. Time pressure cannot replace evidence, and urgency cannot remove the need for food-safety controls.
CH01_SC06_005_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC07_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC07_001_NARRATOR.text: Hamad Al Zaabi, a field investigator in applied chemistry, arrives at the station carrying a tablet and a compact evidence kit.
CH01_SC07_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC07_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH01_SC07_002_HAMAD.text: I understand we have three sealed containers, three unidentified white powders, and three possible materials.
CH01_SC07_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC07_003_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH01_SC07_003_FATIMA.text: Correct. Nothing has been opened or used.
CH01_SC07_003_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC07_004_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH01_SC07_004_HAMAD.text: Good. That means the potential hazard has been contained. Now we can investigate without creating unnecessary exposure.
CH01_SC07_004_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC07_005_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH01_SC07_005_HAMAD.text: I need your help. From this point forward, you are our junior food chemistry investigator. Your task is to examine the evidence, identify what the tests can and cannot prove, and recommend the safest final action.
CH01_SC07_005_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC07_006_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH01_SC07_006_HAMAD.text: Do not rely on appearance. Do not rely on assumptions. Follow the evidence.
CH01_SC07_006_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH01_SC07_007_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH01_SC07_007_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_DEC01_001_HAMAD.text: Three powders may look identical while behaving very differently at the molecular level. We need a test that produces measurable and comparable evidence. What should we do first?
CH02_DEC01_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_002_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_DEC01_002_NARRATOR.text: Review the four possible actions. Select the method that is safe, controlled, and scientifically useful.
CH02_DEC01_002_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_APPEARANCE_1_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH02_DEC01_APPEARANCE_1_MARIAM.text: They are all white. Any slight visual difference could come from lighting, particle size, or the container itself.
CH02_DEC01_APPEARANCE_1_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_APPEARANCE_2_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_DEC01_APPEARANCE_2_HAMAD.text: Correct. Color alone cannot establish chemical identity. Choose a method that produces measurable evidence.
CH02_DEC01_APPEARANCE_2_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_CORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_DEC01_CORRECT_HAMAD.text: Good choice. Conductivity can help us determine whether dissolved particles are able to carry electrical charge. We will test each sample separately under identical conditions.
CH02_DEC01_CORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_MIX_1_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_DEC01_MIX_1_HAMAD.text: Mixing them would destroy the separation between the samples and reduce the value of the evidence. It could also create an unnecessary reaction or contamination risk.
CH02_DEC01_MIX_1_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_MIX_2_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_DEC01_MIX_2_HAMAD.text: Keep each sample separate. Try again.
CH02_DEC01_MIX_2_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_TASTE_1_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_DEC01_TASTE_1_HAMAD.text: Stop. We never taste an unidentified substance. A familiar appearance does not prove that a substance is safe, food-grade, or uncontaminated.
CH02_DEC01_TASTE_1_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_DEC01_TASTE_2_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH02_DEC01_TASTE_2_FATIMA.text: The containers remain sealed. Select a non-consumptive test.
CH02_DEC01_TASTE_2_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC08_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC08_001_NARRATOR.text: The first rejected method is visual identification.
CH02_SC08_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC08_002_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH02_SC08_002_MARIAM.text: Even under the inspection light, the powders appear almost identical. We cannot identify them merely by deciding that one looks brighter or whiter.
CH02_SC08_002_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC08_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC08_003_HAMAD.text: Exactly. Appearance is an observation, but it is not a unique chemical signature. Different substances can share the same color, texture, and general physical form.
CH02_SC08_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC08_004_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC08_004_NARRATOR.text: The investigation must move beyond what the eye can see.
CH02_SC08_004_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC09_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC09_001_NARRATOR.text: A second possible shortcut is tasting. Hamad prevents that action before any container is opened.
CH02_SC09_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC09_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC09_002_HAMAD.text: Never use your body as a chemical detector. Tasting an unidentified substance is not a valid or acceptable investigative method.
CH02_SC09_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC09_003_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH02_SC09_003_SAEED.text: Even if all three candidates are normally used in food?
CH02_SC09_003_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC09_004_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC09_004_HAMAD.text: The candidate list does not verify the actual contents, purity, source, or condition of these containers. Until those questions are addressed, no one tastes anything.
CH02_SC09_004_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC09_005_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH02_SC09_005_FATIMA.text: Safety procedures remain in effect, regardless of the deadline.
CH02_SC09_005_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC10_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC10_001_NARRATOR.text: A third shortcut would be to combine the powders. That would make reliable comparison impossible.
CH02_SC10_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC10_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC10_002_HAMAD.text: Each sample is a separate source of information. If we combine them, we lose the ability to connect a measurement to a specific container.
CH02_SC10_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC10_003_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH02_SC10_003_MARIAM.text: So even before testing, preserving the evidence matters.
CH02_SC10_003_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC10_004_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC10_004_HAMAD.text: Precisely. Reliable science depends not only on the instrument, but also on how the samples are controlled.
CH02_SC10_004_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC11_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC11_001_NARRATOR.text: The competition station becomes a temporary scientific investigation workspace. The three samples stay separated. Clean beakers, water, measuring tools, a conductivity probe, and a pH probe are prepared.
CH02_SC11_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC11_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC11_002_HAMAD.text: To compare the samples fairly, every preparation condition must be the same. In this simulation, each solution is prepared using zero point one zero grams of material per one hundred millilitres of water, at twenty-five degrees Celsius.
CH02_SC11_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC11_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC11_003_HAMAD.text: These are standardized educational simulation conditions. The values are designed to help us compare evidence within this investigation. They are not universal laboratory specifications for every real-world situation.
CH02_SC11_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC11_004_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC11_004_NARRATOR.text: Equal concentration, equal water volume, equal temperature, and separate equipment handling allow the three results to be meaningfully compared.
CH02_SC11_004_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC12_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC12_001_HAMAD.text: Before testing the samples, we need a control measurement.
CH02_SC12_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC12_002_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH02_SC12_002_MARIAM.text: A measurement using only the water?
CH02_SC12_002_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC12_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC12_003_HAMAD.text: Correct. The water-only control tells us the background conductivity of the system before any sample is added.
CH02_SC12_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC12_004_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC12_004_NARRATOR.text: The probe is placed into the water-only control.
CH02_SC12_004_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC12_005_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC12_005_SYSTEM.text: Water-only control: two microsiemens per centimetre.
CH02_SC12_005_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC12_006_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC12_006_HAMAD.text: Calibration and controls help us interpret the later measurements. Without a reference point, a number can be misleading.
CH02_SC12_006_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC13_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC13_001_HAMAD.text: Select Sample A and begin the first conductivity measurement.
CH02_SC13_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC13_002_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC13_002_NARRATOR.text: The probe is rinsed, placed into the prepared solution, and allowed to stabilize.
CH02_SC13_002_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC13_003_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC13_003_SYSTEM.text: Sample A conductivity: four microsiemens per centimetre.
CH02_SC13_003_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC13_004_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH02_SC13_004_MARIAM.text: That is only slightly above the water control.
CH02_SC13_004_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC13_005_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC13_005_HAMAD.text: Correct. Sample A produces very few mobile charged particles under these simulation conditions.
CH02_SC13_005_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC13_006_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC13_006_HAMAD.text: Record the observation, but do not identify the sample yet. One measurement is evidence, not a complete conclusion.
CH02_SC13_006_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC14_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC14_001_NARRATOR.text: The same procedure is repeated for Samples B and C.
CH02_SC14_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC14_002_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC14_002_SYSTEM.text: Sample B conductivity: one thousand one hundred microsiemens per centimetre.
CH02_SC14_002_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC14_003_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC14_003_SYSTEM.text: Sample C conductivity: one thousand nine hundred and thirty microsiemens per centimetre.
CH02_SC14_003_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC14_004_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH02_SC14_004_SAEED.text: Those readings are much higher than Sample A.
CH02_SC14_004_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC14_005_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC14_005_HAMAD.text: Yes. Samples B and C produce solutions containing far more mobile charged particles than Sample A.
CH02_SC14_005_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC14_006_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH02_SC14_006_MARIAM.text: Does that prove Sample A is sugar?
CH02_SC14_006_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC14_007_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC14_007_HAMAD.text: It supports that possibility within our candidate set. But conductivity alone does not provide a unique chemical identity.
CH02_SC14_007_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC14_008_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC14_008_NARRATOR.text: The first evidence pattern is now visible. Sample A has very low conductivity. Samples B and C conduct much more strongly. But two samples still remain unresolved.
CH02_SC14_008_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC15_001_HAMAD.text: To understand the readings, we need to examine what happens at the atomic level.
CH02_SC15_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_002_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC15_002_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC15_003_HAMAD.text: A neutral sodium atom has eleven protons and eleven electrons. When sodium loses one electron, it has one more proton than electrons. It becomes a positively charged sodium ion.
CH02_SC15_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_004_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC15_004_SYSTEM.text: Sodium atom: eleven protons and eleven electrons. Sodium ion: eleven protons and ten electrons. Net charge: positive one.
CH02_SC15_004_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_005_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC15_005_HAMAD.text: Chlorine behaves differently. A neutral chlorine atom has seventeen protons and seventeen electrons. When chlorine gains an electron, it has one more electron than protons. It becomes a negatively charged chloride ion.
CH02_SC15_005_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_006_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC15_006_SYSTEM.text: Chlorine atom: seventeen protons and seventeen electrons. Chloride ion: seventeen protons and eighteen electrons. Net charge: negative one.
CH02_SC15_006_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_007_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC15_007_HAMAD.text: Opposite charges attract. This electrostatic attraction forms an ionic bond.
CH02_SC15_007_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_008_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC15_008_NARRATOR.text: When sodium chloride dissolves in water, sodium and chloride ions separate and move through the solution. Because the ions can carry charge, the solution conducts electricity.
CH02_SC15_008_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC15_009_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC15_009_HAMAD.text: Sucrose also dissolves in water, but it remains mainly as electrically neutral molecules. Dissolving does not automatically mean forming ions.
CH02_SC15_009_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC16_001_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH02_SC16_001_MARIAM.text: Sample A has very low conductivity, but Samples B and C both conduct strongly. We still cannot tell which one is baking soda and which one is salt.
CH02_SC16_001_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC16_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC16_002_HAMAD.text: That is an excellent observation. Our first test separated one evidence pattern from the other two, but it did not provide a complete identification.
CH02_SC16_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC16_003_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH02_SC16_003_SAEED.text: So we need another independent property.
CH02_SC16_003_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC16_004_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC16_004_HAMAD.text: Exactly. High-quality conclusions rarely depend on a single observation. We need evidence that distinguishes the chemical behavior of Samples B and C.
CH02_SC16_004_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC17_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC17_001_HAMAD.text: The next test measures P H. Each prepared solution is tested separately using the same controlled procedure.
CH02_SC17_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC17_002_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC17_002_NARRATOR.text: A P H value near seven is neutral under these simulation conditions. A value above seven indicates basic behavior.
CH02_SC17_002_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC17_003_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC17_003_SYSTEM.text: Sample A P H: seven point zero. Sample B P H: eight point three. Sample C P H: seven point zero.
CH02_SC17_003_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC17_004_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH02_SC17_004_MARIAM.text: Sample B is mildly basic. Samples A and C are neutral in this simulation.
CH02_SC17_004_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC17_005_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC17_005_HAMAD.text: Correct. The P H result gives us a second independent clue. But we can strengthen the identification further.
CH02_SC17_005_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC18_001_HAMAD.text: We will now perform a controlled virtual reaction using a dilute acid and separate portions of each prepared sample.
CH02_SC18_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_002_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH02_SC18_002_FATIMA.text: The original containers remain sealed and isolated.
CH02_SC18_002_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC18_003_HAMAD.text: Correct. This is a controlled simulation, not an invitation to reproduce the procedure without proper supervision and equipment.
CH02_SC18_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_004_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC18_004_SYSTEM.text: Sample A: no visible gas formation.
CH02_SC18_004_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_005_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC18_005_SYSTEM.text: Sample B: carbon dioxide gas detected.
CH02_SC18_005_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_006_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH02_SC18_006_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_007_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC18_007_HAMAD.text: That reaction is consistent with the presence of hydrogen carbonate ions.
CH02_SC18_007_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_008_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC18_008_SYSTEM.text: Sample C: no visible gas formation.
CH02_SC18_008_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC18_009_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC18_009_HAMAD.text: We now have three evidence categories: conductivity, P H, and controlled reaction behavior.
CH02_SC18_009_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC19_001_HAMAD.text: Review the complete evidence before assigning an identity to any sample.
CH02_SC19_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_002_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC19_002_NARRATOR.text: Sample A produced very low conductivity, had a P H of seven point zero, and did not release gas during the virtual acid test. Sample B produced high conductivity, had a P H of eight point three, and released carbon dioxide. Sample C produced the highest conductivity, had a P H of seven point zero, and did not release gas.
CH02_SC19_002_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC19_003_HAMAD.text: Use the combined evidence to identify sucrose, sodium hydrogen carbonate, and sodium chloride.
CH02_SC19_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_A_OK_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC19_A_OK_HAMAD.text: Supported. Sucrose is a molecular substance. In this simulation, it dissolves without producing a large concentration of mobile ions, resulting in very low conductivity.
CH02_SC19_A_OK_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_A_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC19_A_SYSTEM.text: Sample A: sucrose, or table sugar.
CH02_SC19_A_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_B_OK_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC19_B_OK_HAMAD.text: Supported. Sample B conducts, shows mildly basic behavior, and releases carbon dioxide in the controlled virtual acid test.
CH02_SC19_B_OK_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_B_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC19_B_SYSTEM.text: Sample B: sodium hydrogen carbonate, or baking soda.
CH02_SC19_B_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_COMPLETE_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH02_SC19_COMPLETE_NARRATOR.text: The scientific identification is complete. Sample A is consistent with sucrose. Sample B is consistent with sodium hydrogen carbonate. Sample C is consistent with sodium chloride. The mystery appears to be solved. But the most important decision has not yet been made.
CH02_SC19_COMPLETE_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_C_OK_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC19_C_OK_HAMAD.text: Supported. Sodium chloride forms mobile ions in solution, resulting in high conductivity. In this simulation, it remains near neutral and does not produce carbon dioxide in the acid test.
CH02_SC19_C_OK_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_C_SYSTEM.speaker: SYSTEM
CH02_SC19_C_SYSTEM.text: Sample C: sodium chloride, or table salt.
CH02_SC19_C_SYSTEM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH02_SC19_WRONG_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH02_SC19_WRONG_HAMAD.text: That assignment does not match all three observations. Review the conductivity, P H, and virtual acid-test results together. A defensible identification must explain every relevant observation, not only one of them.
CH02_SC19_WRONG_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC20_001_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH03_SC20_001_MARIAM.text: We know which sample is sugar, and we know which sample is baking soda. Can we return them to the preparation station?
CH03_SC20_001_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC20_002_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH03_SC20_002_SAEED.text: If the evidence supports their identities, we could still finish the dessert.
CH03_SC20_002_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC20_003_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH03_SC20_003_FATIMA.text: Before I authorize anything, I need a clear safety recommendation.
CH03_SC20_003_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC20_004_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH03_SC20_004_NARRATOR.text: The team now faces a question that is larger than chemical identification. The tests support the identity of each material within the limited candidate set. But identifying a compound and verifying a food ingredient are not the same task.
CH03_SC20_004_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC21_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH03_SC21_001_HAMAD.text: Our results support the conclusion that Sample A is sucrose, Sample B is sodium hydrogen carbonate, and Sample C is sodium chloride.
CH03_SC21_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC21_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH03_SC21_002_HAMAD.text: But consider what our tests did not establish.
CH03_SC21_002_HAMAD.direction: Pause one second after this line.
CH03_SC21_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC21_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH03_SC21_003_HAMAD.text: Did we verify where the powders came from? Did we verify that they were manufactured and stored as food-grade ingredients? Did we verify that the containers were not contaminated before arriving here? Did we establish an unbroken chain of custody?
CH03_SC21_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC21_004_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH03_SC21_004_MARIAM.text: No. We only investigated their chemical behavior.
CH03_SC21_004_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC21_005_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH03_SC21_005_HAMAD.text: Correct. Chemical identification asks, “What substance is this?” Food-safety verification asks, “Is this documented, traceable material suitable for human consumption?” A chemical identity does not automatically answer the second question.
CH03_SC21_005_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC21_006_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH03_SC21_006_FATIMA.text: So even a scientifically supported identity does not authorize us to use an ingredient with an unverified source.
CH03_SC21_006_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC21_007_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH03_SC21_007_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH03_SC22_001_NARRATOR.text: The evidence is complete. The responsibility now belongs to the investigator.
CH03_SC22_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH03_SC22_002_HAMAD.text: Choose the action you can defend scientifically and professionally. Your decision must account for both the laboratory evidence and the limits of that evidence.
CH03_SC22_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH03_SC22_003_HAMAD.text: Select one recommendation. Then provide a written justification of at least sixty characters and cite at least two observations from the investigation.
CH03_SC22_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_004_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH03_SC22_004_NARRATOR.text: Consider the consequences carefully. Identifying a substance is not the same as verifying that it is safe to serve.
CH03_SC22_004_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_005_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH03_SC22_005_HAMAD.text: When you are ready, commit your decision.
CH03_SC22_005_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_OPTION_A_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH03_SC22_OPTION_A_NARRATOR.text: Option A: Document the scientific findings, isolate the unidentified containers, and replace them with new, sealed, traceable food ingredients.
CH03_SC22_OPTION_A_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_OPTION_B_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH03_SC22_OPTION_B_NARRATOR.text: Option B: Use the powder with the lowest conductivity because it is likely to be sugar.
CH03_SC22_OPTION_B_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_OPTION_C_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH03_SC22_OPTION_C_NARRATOR.text: Option C: Ask someone to taste the powders to confirm their identities quickly.
CH03_SC22_OPTION_C_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH03_SC22_OPTION_D_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH03_SC22_OPTION_D_NARRATOR.text: Option D: Return the powders to preparation based on which one appears whitest.
CH03_SC22_OPTION_D_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_A_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_A_001_NARRATOR.text: You choose to document the scientific findings, isolate all three unidentified containers, and replace them with new, sealed ingredients from a traceable food source.
CH04_END_A_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_A_002_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH04_END_A_002_FATIMA.text: The original containers will remain isolated. They will not return to food preparation.
CH04_END_A_002_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_A_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_A_003_HAMAD.text: I’ll record the supported identities and the limits of our investigation. The evidence tells us what the powders are consistent with, but it does not establish food provenance or freedom from contamination.
CH04_END_A_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_A_004_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH04_END_A_004_MARIAM.text: The replacement sugar and baking soda are sealed, identified, and verified. We can continue safely.
CH04_END_A_004_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_A_005_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH04_END_A_005_SAEED.text: We lost a little time, but we did not risk serving an unverified ingredient.
CH04_END_A_005_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_A_006_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_A_006_NARRATOR.text: Preparation resumes using new, documented ingredients. The unidentified containers remain sealed and separated from the food area. No unknown material is served.
CH04_END_A_006_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_A_007_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_A_007_HAMAD.text: Strong decision. You used the evidence correctly and respected its limits. Scientific confidence does not mean claiming more than the investigation can prove.
CH04_END_A_007_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_A_008_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_A_008_NARRATOR.text: Outcome: the evidence is documented, the unverified containers are isolated, verified replacements are used, and preparation resumes safely.
CH04_END_A_008_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_B_001_NARRATOR.text: You choose to use the powder with the lowest conductivity because the data suggest that it is sucrose.
CH04_END_B_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_002_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH04_END_B_002_MARIAM.text: The conductivity result supports the sugar identification. But do we know where the powder came from?
CH04_END_B_002_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_003_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH04_END_B_003_FATIMA.text: No. We cannot verify its source, food-grade status, storage history, or freedom from contamination.
CH04_END_B_003_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_004_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_B_004_HAMAD.text: Low conductivity helps distinguish sucrose from the two ionic candidates in this investigation. It does not verify that the material is suitable for consumption.
CH04_END_B_004_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_005_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH04_END_B_005_FATIMA.text: Preparation must stop. Any batch connected to an unverified ingredient must be discarded.
CH04_END_B_005_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_006_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH04_END_B_006_SAEED.text: We tried to save time, but the missing verification has cost us more time.
CH04_END_B_006_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_007_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_B_007_NARRATOR.text: The affected preparation is discarded, and the final round is delayed while verified ingredients are obtained.
CH04_END_B_007_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_008_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_B_008_HAMAD.text: The evidence was interpreted too broadly. A conductivity reading can support chemical identification. It cannot establish source, purity, or food safety on its own.
CH04_END_B_008_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_B_009_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_B_009_NARRATOR.text: Outcome: preparation stops, the affected batch is discarded, and the unknown containers remain unauthorized for food use.
CH04_END_B_009_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_C_001_NARRATOR.text: You suggest tasting the powders as a quick way to confirm their identities.
CH04_END_C_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_C_002_HAMAD.text: Stop. Do not open the container.
CH04_END_C_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_003_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH04_END_C_003_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_004_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_C_004_HAMAD.text: Tasting is not an acceptable test for an unidentified material. It creates direct exposure while providing weak and subjective evidence.
CH04_END_C_004_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_005_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH04_END_C_005_FATIMA.text: The containers will be moved farther from the food-preparation area. No one will taste, smell, or handle the contents.
CH04_END_C_005_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_006_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH04_END_C_006_MARIAM.text: We will wait for verified replacement ingredients.
CH04_END_C_006_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_007_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_C_007_NARRATOR.text: The unsafe action is prevented before any container is opened. No one is exposed, but additional preparation time is lost while the team returns to the correct safety procedure.
CH04_END_C_007_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_008_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_C_008_HAMAD.text: Safe investigation requires knowing what not to do. Familiar appearance and expected ingredients never justify tasting an unknown substance.
CH04_END_C_008_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_C_009_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_C_009_NARRATOR.text: Outcome: tasting is prevented, the samples remain sealed, and the team must obtain verified replacements.
CH04_END_C_009_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_D_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_D_001_NARRATOR.text: You choose to identify the powders according to which one appears whitest.
CH04_END_D_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_D_002_MARIAM.speaker: MARIAM
CH04_END_D_002_MARIAM.text: Under the inspection light, they still look almost identical.
CH04_END_D_002_MARIAM.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_D_003_SAEED.speaker: SAEED
CH04_END_D_003_SAEED.text: I cannot defend one visual choice over another.
CH04_END_D_003_SAEED.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_D_004_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_D_004_HAMAD.text: Whiteness is not a unique chemical property. Lighting, particle size, surface reflection, and the container itself can all affect visual appearance.
CH04_END_D_004_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_D_005_FATIMA.speaker: FATIMA
CH04_END_D_005_FATIMA.text: The identities have not been established through the proposed method. The containers cannot return to food preparation.
CH04_END_D_005_FATIMA.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_D_006_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_D_006_NARRATOR.text: The team must restart using ingredients with clear labels and traceable sources. The attempt to save time through appearance creates further delay.
CH04_END_D_006_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_D_007_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH04_END_D_007_HAMAD.text: A conclusion is only as strong as the evidence supporting it. Visual similarity cannot establish chemical identity or food safety.
CH04_END_D_007_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH04_END_D_008_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH04_END_D_008_NARRATOR.text: Outcome: visual verification fails, preparation remains paused, and documented replacement ingredients are required.
CH04_END_D_008_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q01_CORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q01_CORRECT_HAMAD.text: Correct. Sodium loses one electron. It then has eleven protons and ten electrons, producing a net charge of positive one.
CH05_Q01_CORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q01_INCORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q01_INCORRECT_HAMAD.text: Not quite. A positive ion forms when an atom has fewer electrons than protons. Sodium becomes positive by losing one electron.
CH05_Q01_INCORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q01_QUESTION_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_Q01_QUESTION_NARRATOR.text: How does a neutral sodium atom become a positively charged sodium ion?
CH05_Q01_QUESTION_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q02_CORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q02_CORRECT_HAMAD.text: Correct. Chlorine gains one electron. It then has seventeen protons and eighteen electrons, producing a net charge of negative one.
CH05_Q02_CORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q02_INCORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q02_INCORRECT_HAMAD.text: Review the relationship between protons and electrons. Chlorine becomes negatively charged by gaining one electron.
CH05_Q02_INCORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q02_QUESTION_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_Q02_QUESTION_NARRATOR.text: How does a neutral chlorine atom become a negatively charged chloride ion?
CH05_Q02_QUESTION_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q03_CORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q03_CORRECT_HAMAD.text: Correct. Sodium chloride separates into mobile sodium and chloride ions in water. Those charged particles carry electrical current through the solution.
CH05_Q03_CORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q03_INCORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q03_INCORRECT_HAMAD.text: Conductivity is not caused simply by the presence of water or by the white color of the solid. It depends on mobile charged particles in the solution.
CH05_Q03_INCORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q03_QUESTION_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_Q03_QUESTION_NARRATOR.text: Why does an aqueous sodium chloride solution conduct electricity?
CH05_Q03_QUESTION_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q04_CORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q04_CORRECT_HAMAD.text: Correct. Sucrose dissolves mainly as neutral molecules and does not produce the same concentration of mobile ions as sodium chloride.
CH05_Q04_CORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q04_INCORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q04_INCORRECT_HAMAD.text: Dissolving and ionizing are not the same process. Sucrose can dissolve while remaining mainly as neutral molecules.
CH05_Q04_INCORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q04_QUESTION_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_Q04_QUESTION_NARRATOR.text: Why does a sucrose solution conduct electricity much less effectively than a sodium chloride solution under the simulation conditions?
CH05_Q04_QUESTION_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q05_CORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q05_CORRECT_HAMAD.text: Correct. A single test may be shared by different substances. Independent evidence increases confidence and helps distinguish between candidates with similar properties.
CH05_Q05_CORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q05_INCORRECT_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_Q05_INCORRECT_HAMAD.text: Conductivity showed that Samples B and C both produced mobile ions, but it did not uniquely distinguish them. Additional evidence was required.
CH05_Q05_INCORRECT_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_Q05_QUESTION_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_Q05_QUESTION_NARRATOR.text: Why was it necessary to combine conductivity, P H, and controlled reaction evidence?
CH05_Q05_QUESTION_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_QUIZ_INTRO_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_QUIZ_INTRO_NARRATOR.text: Answer five questions about ions, conductivity, molecular substances, and evidence-based identification. You need at least four correct answers out of five to earn the Ionic Evidence Investigator achievement.
CH05_QUIZ_INTRO_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_REFLECTION_001_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_REFLECTION_001_NARRATOR.text: You have seen the consequences of your decision. Now reflect on the reasoning that produced it.
CH05_REFLECTION_001_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_REFLECTION_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_REFLECTION_002_HAMAD.text: Explain what you learned from the outcome. Refer to at least one piece of scientific evidence from the investigation. State what you would keep or change if you faced a similar decision again.
CH05_REFLECTION_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_REFLECTION_003_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_REFLECTION_003_NARRATOR.text: What evidence influenced your decision? What did the tests establish? What remained unknown? How did your decision protect, or fail to protect, the people who would consume the food?
CH05_REFLECTION_003_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC27_001_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_SC27_001_HAMAD.text: Today, you investigated the invisible chemistry behind familiar everyday materials.
CH05_SC27_001_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC27_002_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_SC27_002_HAMAD.text: You observed that substances can look alike and still behave differently. You used conductivity to investigate the presence of mobile charged particles. You used P H and controlled reaction behavior to distinguish between two ionic substances. And you combined independent observations instead of relying on one result.
CH05_SC27_002_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC27_003_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_SC27_003_HAMAD.text: But the most important lesson appeared after the substances were identified.
CH05_SC27_003_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC27_004_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_SC27_004_HAMAD.text: Knowing a chemical identity does not automatically verify source, purity, storage history, or suitability for human consumption.
CH05_SC27_004_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC27_005_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_SC27_005_HAMAD.text: A good investigator follows the evidence. A responsible investigator also recognizes the limits of the evidence. And when public safety is involved, a defensible decision is more important than a fast one.
CH05_SC27_005_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC27_006_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_SC27_006_NARRATOR.text: The investigation is complete. One final assessment remains.
CH05_SC27_006_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC28_PASS_1_NARRATOR.speaker: NARRATOR
CH05_SC28_PASS_1_NARRATOR.text: Assessment complete. You answered at least four of the five questions correctly.
CH05_SC28_PASS_1_NARRATOR.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC28_PASS_2_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_SC28_PASS_2_HAMAD.text: Well done. You have earned the Ionic Evidence Investigator achievement.
CH05_SC28_PASS_2_HAMAD.captionSource: supplied author TXT and matching manifest.csv

CH05_SC28_PASS_3_HAMAD.speaker: HAMAD
CH05_SC28_PASS_3_HAMAD.text: You demonstrated that scientific investigation requires accurate observation, controlled comparison, independent evidence, and responsible interpretation.
